chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Frames the Zuowandao & Loses His Own Head – Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 417
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang kills a Heavenly Office Overseer while disguised as Red Center, and escapes the capital. But when he stops running, he discovers his own head is gone.
og_title: The Mad Retreat: A Chapter of False Flags and Vanishing Heads
og_description: Li Huowang frames the Zuowandao for murder in a wild escape. The chaos pays off—but the price is his own missing head.
twitter_title: Li Huowang's Escape: Victory and a Vanished Head
twitter_description: A tactical retreat turns into existential horror. What does it mean when a headless man can still think?

lore_anchors.definition: A corrupted celestial almanac that determines auspicious and inauspicious days; in the Dao-Twisted World, it functions as a powerful and chaotic ritual artifact.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body; they hunt rogue cultivators and manage supernatural disasters on an imperial scale.

A secret society whose name means "The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness," a perversion of a Daoist meditative concept; they are liars and tricksters dedicated to spreading confusion and chaos for their own amusement.
A high-ranking alias within the Zuowandao hierarchy, named after a mahjong tile. Li Huowang masquerades as this to frame them for murder.
A fable referenced by Li Huowang; he weaponizes the Zuowandao's history of lies, knowing no one will believe them now, even if they tell the truth.

cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a corrupted celestial calendar used as a powerful ritual artifact. Li Huowang steals it to use as bait and as a weapon in his false-flag operation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang kill the Overseer?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He killed the Overseer while disguised as a Zuowandao member to frame them for the murder, forcing the Office and the Zuowandao into an all-out war.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Li Huowang's head really gone?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes, at the end of the chapter, his hands find only empty space above his neck. His head is physically missing, yet he is still alive and thinking, marking a new level of body-horror in his cultivation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How is Li Huowang still alive without a head?
cultural_notes_faq.a: This is the chapter's central mystery. It implies his cultivation, his parasitic passenger Li Sui, or his "Heart-Element" constitution has fundamentally altered his physiology, allowing him to function without a head.
In this context, it is a high-ranking alias within the Zuowandao. Li Huowang is impersonating a member named Red Center to perform the false flag attack.
